newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded gasoline prices ease.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded gasoline prices ease.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline prices eased on steady differentials against falling futures prices on Tuesday, traders said.
Unleaded and diesel prices were expected to continue tracking NYMEX front-month futures, which moved more than one cent a gallon lower in morning trade.
Front-month heating oil was driving the NYMEX sell-off on reports of above-normal temperatures expected in the U.S. Northeast, the world's largest heating oil market.
"The Merc is driving the (spot) market lower, and I think differentials might ease up a bit, too," one trader said.
Prompt low sulphur diesel was bid 6.50 cents a gallon under NYMEX January heating oil in Chicago and 3.25 cents under in Group Three.
"Low sulphur is driving the whole market lower," one Chicago trader said.
High sulphur diesel remained 7.0/6.50 cents a gallon under the print in Chicago and 6.50/6.0 cents a gallon under the print in Group Three, traders said.
Prompt unleaded gasoline was talked 2.0/1.75 cents a gallon under the print in Chicago and 3.25/3.0 cents under in Grour Three. Later deliveries were 0.50 cent weaker in both markets.
